newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Talks on Cyprus dispute due in mid June - envoy.
newsitem.headline: Talks on Cyprus dispute due in mid June - envoy.

text.p: United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan will decide by the end of May whether to invite rival sides in divided Cyprus to face-to-face talks on a political settlement, a U.N. official said on Wednesday.

Annan plans to open talks next month between the leaders of the Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot communities aimed at reuniting the island under a federal system -- a goal that has eluded the United Nations for more than two decades.

Sir Kieran Prendergast, the U.N. Under Secretary-General for Political Affairs, who was in Cyprus for talks with the leaders of the two sides, said Annan would take a firm decision on whether to issue the invitation at the end of May.
If the talks do get off the ground, it would be the first known encounter of President Glafcos Clerides, the Greek Cypriot leader, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash, for nearly three years.

"The Secretary-general's decision is that the talks should resume by the middle of this year," said Prendergast, who said he would be reporting back to the secretary-general on the outcome of his contacts on the island.
"I would guess his decision (whether to issue an invitation) would be taken about the end of May," Prendergast said.
Turkey invaded northern Cyprus in 1974 in response to a brief coup engineered by the military junta ruling Athens at the time.
A Turkish Cypriot breakaway state, declared in 1983, is a base for 30,000 mainland Turkish troops. It is recognised only by Ankara. The Greek Cypriot-led government is internationally recognised.
The U.N. resident representative, Gustave Feissel, has been conducting a series of proximity talks between the two sides since early March in preparation of the resumption of direct talks.

Peace efforts suffered a serious setback last year after the killings of four Greek Cypriots by Turks or Turkish Cypriots along the U.N. patrolled buffer zone separating the two communities, and the fatal shooting of a Turkish Cypriot sentry and the wounding of another.
